6.2 This PDA shall not create the relationship of partnership joint venture and, or, agent relationships between the Parties, nor authorise the parties to make or enter into any commitments for or on behalf of another party.

6.3 Nothing contained or implied in this PDA or any consent or approval granted pursuant to this PDA shall prejudice or affect the rights powers duties and obligations of the Parties in the exercise of their respective statutory functions and such rights powers duties and obligations may be as fully and effectually exercised as if the relevant Party was not a party to this PDA and any approval consent direction or authority given by the relevant Party as local or statutory authority (as the case may be) shall not be or be deemed to be an approval consent direction or authority given under this PDA and vice versa.

In witness whereof, the undersigned have signed duplicates of the present PDA on behalf of respective institutions and agree that nothing express or implied in this agreement creates any legally binding obligations on either party. Each Party shall keep one copy of the originals.

Signed for and on behalf of Homes and Communities Agency (Homes England)

Signed for and on behalf of National Housing Bank

Signed for and on behalf of Liverpool City Region Combined Authority

Schedule

1. Confidentiality

1.1 In this clause the following words and expressions have the following meaning:

Confidential Information means the terms of this PDA and all information whether oral or written (on whatever medium stored) relating this PDA disclosed or made available, directly or indirectly one party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers to the other party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers but excludes any information which:

(i) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, publicly available; (ii) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, available to the Recipient from a person who, to the Recipient’s knowledge, is not under any confidential obligation in respect of that information; or (iii) has been independently acquired by a Party without breaching any of their respective obligations in this PDA.

1.2 Each Party recognises that under this PDA it may receive Confidential Information belonging to the other.

1.3 Each Party agrees to treat all Confidential Information belonging to the other as confidential and not to disclose such Confidential Information or any other confidential information relating to each other arising or coming to its attention in the course of this PDA to any third party without the prior written consent of the other Party and agrees not to use such Confidential Information for any purpose other than that for which it is supplied under this PDA.

1.4 The obligations of confidence referred to in Clause 1.3 shall not apply to any Confidential Information which:

(a) is in, or which comes into, the public domain otherwise than by reason of a breach of this this PDA or of any other duty of confidentiality relating to that information; or

(b) is obtained from a third party without that third party being under an obligation (express or implied) to keep the information confidential; or

(c) is lawfully in the possession of the other Party before the date of this this PDA and in respect of which that Party is not under an existing obligation of confidentiality; or

(d) is independently developed without access to the Confidential Information of the other Party.

1.5 Each Party will be permitted to disclose Confidential Information to the extent that it is required to do so:

(a) to enable the disclosing party to perform its obligations under this this PDA; or

(b) by any applicable law or by a court, arbitral or administrative tribunal in the course of proceedings before it including without limitation any requirement for disclosure under Freedom of Information Laws as defined in clause 3) and the Parties acknowledge that any lists or schedules provided by it outlining Confidential Information are of indicative value only and that the other party may nevertheless be obliged to disclose such confidential information; or

(c) by any regulatory body (including any investment exchange) acting in the course of proceedings before it or acting in the course of its duties; or

(d) in order to give proper instructions to any professional adviser of that Party who also has an obligation to keep any such Confidential Information confidential.

1.6 The Parties shall ensure that all Confidential Information obtained from the other Party under or in connection with this PDA:-

(a) is given only to such of its employees, professional advisors or consultants engaged to advise it in connection with this PDA as is strictly necessary for the performance of this PDA and only to the extent necessary for the performance of this PDA;

(b) is treated as confidential and not disclosed (without Homes England’s prior written approval) or used by any such staff or professional advisors or consultants otherwise than for the purposes of this PDA and in all instances such third parties are subject to a signed confidentiality undertaking.

1.7 Notwithstanding any other provision of this PDA, nothing in this agreement shall prevent Homes England:

(a) disclosing any Confidential Information for the purpose of:

(i) the examination and certification of its accounts; or

(ii) any examination pursuant to section 6(1) of the National Audit Act 1983 of the economy, efficiency and effectiveness with which Homes England has used its resources; or

(b) disclosing any Confidential Information to any other department, office or agency of the Crown provided that in disclosing such Confidential Information pursuant to this paragraph (b), it discloses only the information which is necessary for the purpose concerned and requires that the information is treated in confidence.

4.22 The partnership will seek to:

realise the LCR’s ambition to become a national centre of excellence for industrialised construction and housing innovation including through the IDCC programme and local pull-through plan

support the IDCC programme’s priorities and local pull-through plan

strengthen the capacity and capability of local authorities, developers and delivery partners to bring forward complex housing and regeneration schemes

align housing delivery with skills, employment and economic development programmes to maximise local economic benefits and create pathways into high-quality jobs, including adopting recommendations from Alan Milburn’s review

work with local authorities, colleges, universities, industry partners and government to address skills shortages and develop the future workforce required to deliver the City Region’s growth ambitions

identify opportunities to test and scale innovative approaches to delivery, infrastructure provision and placemaking that can improve productivity and accelerate housing delivery

4.23 Through this Agreement, Homes England will support the LCRCA to ensure that the skills, capacity and innovation required to support long-term housing and regeneration growth are embedded across the LCR, strengthening the foundations for sustainable delivery and creating a model that can be replicated nationally.

5. Next steps: Delivery, governance and implementation

5.1 This new single framework will help to strengthen local capability to support delivery, while recognising a desire to go further in boosting the capacity, expertise and sharing of good practice across the public and private sector partners in the sub-region via a focused programme of activity.

5.2 The JDU will provide greater visibility and accountability to the Mayor, giving the Mayor the control, influence and resources needed to build the homes and places communities require and to hold partners to account for delivery.

5.3 LCRCA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank commit to progressing a joint Delivery Plan outlining key tasks, milestones and resourcing commitments underpinned by a governance framework which delivers on the principles outlined in this PDA.

Partnership commitments

5.4 The parties commit to:

align resources around mayoral priorities

maintain and enhance the LCR’s shared strategic development and investment pipeline

jointly identify and resolve barriers

coordinate stakeholder engagement through the LCR Developer Network

share intelligence and investment planning

support delivery through a dedicated JDU

5.5 This PDA will operate on a 3-year basis and will be reviewed annually to ensure it remains aligned with evolving national policy, mayoral priorities, market conditions and delivery opportunities. The PDA is intended to provide a single framework while retaining sufficient flexibility to respond to changing circumstances and emerging priorities.

Delivery of the PDA will be supported through:

a rolling delivery programme maintained through the JDU, responding to mayoral priorities, interventions and opportunities requiring joint action

a detailed annual Delivery Plan, agreed following approval of the PDA, translating strategic priorities into specific actions, responsibilities, milestones and resource commitments

an annual review process to refresh delivery priorities, resource allocations and pipeline activity without requiring the full PDA to be renegotiated

regular monitoring and performance reporting through the governance and accountability arrangements within this PDA, enabling partners to track progress, identify emerging risks and agree corrective action where required

5.6 The parties acknowledge that successful delivery will require ongoing collaboration between Homes England, the National Housing Bank, LCRCA and wider delivery partners, including local authorities, government departments, infrastructure providers, registered providers, investors and other stakeholders.

Joint Delivery Unit

5.7 The Joint Delivery Unit (JDU) will provide a single delivery interface between the Combined Authority and Homes England and drive implementation of agreed priorities through the following functions:

programme management

opportunity identification

pipeline development

major project delivery

investment coordination

risk management

performance monitoring

Executive summary

This Place Delivery Agreement (PDA) is dated 1 October 2026 and strengthens the relationship between the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority (LCRCA), Homes England and the National Housing Bank (NHB), through an enhanced single delivery framework to accelerate housing delivery, unlock regeneration and underpin the vision of the Liverpool City Region (LCR) Growth Plan to transform productivity across the LCR.

Building on the success of the existing Strategic Place Partnership (SPP), this Agreement represents a step change in the way the 3 organisations work together. It moves beyond collaboration towards co-delivery, bringing together local leadership, national expertise and investment capability behind a shared set of priorities.

At its heart, the Agreement is about empowering the Mayor and local leaders to deliver their housing, regeneration and growth ambitions by bringing decision-making, investment and delivery capability closer to place.

Through this Agreement, the partners commit to:

Delivering LCR’s most significant growth and regeneration opportunities

Prioritising delivery of the North Liverpool Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC), helping unlock around 17,000 homes and supporting the long-term regeneration of Liverpool’s northern waterfront.

Accelerating delivery of Central Station Gateway, supporting around 4,300 homes alongside commercial growth, connectivity improvements and regeneration across 86 acres of the city centre.

Maintaining the existing LCR pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities across all 6 local authority areas with focused activity to accelerate delivery.

Putting housing investment decisions closer to place

Empowering the LCRCA to shape housing investment and delivery priorities across all tenures.

Supporting mayoral influence over affordable housing investment decisions through regionally-delegated Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) Continuous Market Engagement (CME) arrangements.

Aligning Homes England and National Housing Bank activity with the LCR Growth Plan, Housing Strategy and wider regeneration ambitions.

Accelerating social and affordable housing and council house delivery

Ensuring the delivery of the mayoral ambition for around 16,000 social and affordable homes and council homes across the LCR between 2026 and 2036.

Maximising the impact of LCR’s £700 million SAHP indicative spend amount.

Accelerating council housing delivery.

Supporting local authorities, registered providers and delivery partners to enhance, prioritise and deliver the existing LCR Housing Pipeline.

Unlocking investment at scale

Establishing a connected investment ecosystem for housing and regeneration.

Developing a portfolio of financial transactions capable of attracting significant National Housing Bank investment.

Mobilising significantly greater levels of private and institutional investment into housing and regeneration.

Bringing forward projects that cannot be unlocked through traditional grant funding alone.

Building long-term delivery capacity

Establishing the LCR as a national exemplar for housing delivery, regeneration and place-based growth.

Supporting innovation, skills development and industrialised construction.

Strengthening local capability to bring forward complex housing and regeneration projects.

Aligning housing delivery with wider economic growth, employment and productivity ambitions.

Creating a dedicated Joint Delivery Unit

Establishing a Joint Delivery Unit (JDU) as a single delivery structure bringing together LCRCA, Homes England and National Housing Bank expertise.

Committing dedicated Homes England and National Housing Bank staff, including specialist expertise, across:

planning

regeneration

infrastructure

affordable housing

economics

development finance

legal services

market engagement

Providing a single route through which LCRCA can access the full range of Homes England and National Housing Bank delivery tools, expertise, investment capability and powers.

Aligning resources around shared priorities and accelerating the progression of projects from concept to delivery.

Strengthening accountability and governance

Creating significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor.

Establishing strengthened oversight arrangements involving the Mayor, the chairs of Homes England and the National Housing Bank and the chief executives of both organisations.

Delegating day-to-day Homes England and National Housing Bank responsibility for delivery of the Agreement to the Homes England executive director for the North West.

Nominated co-directors from LCRCA and Homes England will lead the JDU.

Introducing quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes.

This Agreement represents an enhanced model of place-based delivery. By combining local leadership, devolved influence, dedicated delivery capability, aligned investment and stronger accountability, the LCRCA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will work together to deliver more homes, unlock regeneration, attract investment and drive long-term economic growth across the LCR.

Commencement and term

This PDA shall commence on the date hereof and shall continue for an initial period of 3 years (subject to an annual review) and shall thereafter continue for such further period or periods as shall be agreed in writing between the parties, Provided Always that any party may give not less than 90 days prior written notice to the others to terminate this PDA at any time.

1. Strategic context: Liverpool City Region’s growth ambitions

Liverpool City Region Growth Plan 2025 to 2035

1.1 The LCR is one of the UK’s major city regions, with a population of just over 1.6 million people.

It comprises the 6 local authority areas of:

Halton

Knowsley

Liverpool
